It would add: this was Bana's first composition; it is written in ornate poetic prose and, as the work of a poet under Harsha's patronage, shows him in an overly favourable light; its first two chapters tell of Bana's own ancestry and early life; it holds the earliest clear reference to chaturanga; the only surviving commentary is the Sanketa of Shankara, a scholar of Kashmir; it was translated into English by Edward Byles Cowell and Frederick William Thomas in 1897; the military historian Kaushik Roy calls it 'historical fiction' with a factually correct foundation.
